title: Vested Property (Arpita Sampatti) Release in Bangladesh: Legal Procedure for Overseas Heirs & NRBs (2026)
metaTitle: Vested Property Return Act Bangladesh: NRB Release Guide 2026
metaDescription: Legal guide for NRBs and overseas heirs to release ancestral land listed under Vested Property (অর্পিত সম্পত্তি). Tribunal petitions, Ka vs Kha schedule, and writs.
keywords: vested property appeal high court bangladesh
heroIntro: For hundreds of thousands of expatriates belonging to minority communities residing in India, the United States, United Kingdom, and Canada, ancestral real estate in Bangladesh remains entangled in the historical web of the **Vested Property Act (formerly Enemy Property Act 1965)**. Millions of acres of legitimate family land were wrongfully gazetted as 'Vested Property' (অর্পিত সম্পত্তি) due to erroneous bureaucratic entries, fraudulent surveys, or malicious local encroachment during the owners' migration or absence. With the enactment of the **Vested Property Return (Amendment) Act 2011 & 2013**, legal heirs have clear statutory mechanisms to recover title and physical possession.

quickAnswer.heading: Vested Property Recovery: Key Principles
points: Determine whether the property is gazetted under 'Ka' Schedule (currently government-controlled) or 'Kha' Schedule (already de-listed and dropped).
Establish that the original owner was a bona fide permanent resident of East Pakistan / Bangladesh and did not migrate to an enemy state during the 1965 Indo-Pak conflict.
Gather unbroken chain-of-title documents: CS, SA, RS Khatians, legacy deeds, and certified Warishan genealogies.
File an original claim petition before the District Vested Property Return Tribunal (অর্পিত সম্পত্তি প্রত্যর্পণ ট্রাইব্যুনাল).
If aggrieved by the Tribunal's judgment, appeal to the Vested Property Return Appellate Tribunal.
Overseas heirs can litigate entirely through an appointed Power of Attorney.

sections.h2: Historical Background: From Enemy Property 1965 to Vested Property
sections.content:
The origin of Vested Property dates back to the Defence of Pakistan Rules 1965 following the September 1965 Indo-Pakistan war, where lands owned by individuals who migrated to India were classified as 'Enemy Property'. After the independence of Bangladesh in 1971, the government promulgated the Vested and Non-Resident Property (Administration) Act 1974, renaming them as 'Vested Property'.

Tragically, dishonest revenue staff routinely categorized the properties of citizens who never left Bangladesh as vested land. To correct this historical injustice, parliament enacted the Vested Property Return Act 2001 (অর্পিত সম্পত্তি প্রত্যর্পণ আইন, ২০০১), with major structural amendments in 2011 and 2013 creating judicial tribunals.

sections.h2: Understanding the Critical Difference: 'Ka' Schedule vs 'Kha' Schedule
sections.content:
Government gazettes divided vested properties into two distinct categories:

  • 'Ka' Schedule (ক-তফসিল): Properties currently in physical possession, custody, or leasehold of the government. To recover these lands, claimants must file an application before the Vested Property Return Tribunal.
  • 'Kha' Schedule (খ-তফসিল): Properties that were not in government possession but were occupied by private citizens or the original owners. Following nationwide protests and the Vested Property Return (Amendment) Act 2013, the government officially cancelled and dropped the Kha Schedule. If your land was in the Kha schedule, it is automatically released, and you can directly apply for e-Namjari mutation at the AC (Land) office without going to the Tribunal.

sections.h2: Who is Eligible to Claim as an Overseas Heir?
sections.content:
Under Section 2(f) and Section 9 of the 2001 Act, an application can be filed by:

  1. The original permanent owner of the property.
  2. The lawful legal successors or heirs (উত্তরাধিকারী) of the original owner according to their personal law of succession.
  3. Even if heirs reside in the USA, UK, Canada, or India, as long as they can trace their lineage back to the recorded owner on the CS/SA Khatian and establish succession, they have full legal standing to petition the Tribunal through a registered Power of Attorney.

sections.h2: Filing a Petition in the Vested Property Return Tribunal
sections.content:
Special Tribunals headed by Senior Assistant Judges or Sub-Judges operate in each district headquarter:

  • The petition must be instituted in the Vested Property Return Tribunal (অর্পিত সম্পত্তি প্রত্যর্পণ ট্রাইব্যুনাল) of the district where the land is located.
  • The Deputy Commissioner (DC) representing the government is named as the primary opposite party.
  • The petition must articulate the erroneous inclusion of the property in the Ka Schedule, set out the ancestral pedigree, and demand release and delivery of possession.

sections.h2: Evidentiary Burden: Documents Required to Prove Title
sections.content:
To secure a release decree, the claimant must present airtight historical evidence:

  • Certified copies of the CS (Cadastral Survey) and SA (State Acquisition) Khatians showing the ancestor's recorded ownership.
  • Original registered title deeds (সাফ কবলা / হেবা দলিল / পিট দলিল) proving legitimate purchase.
  • Succession / Warishan Certificate authenticated by local municipal authorities.
  • Affidavits of local elderly residents confirming the family's uninterrupted physical possession prior to erroneous listing.
  • Up-to-date land tax receipts and boundary sketch maps.

sections.h2: The Appellate Tribunal & Supreme Court High Court Writ Remedies
sections.content:
If the District Tribunal rejects your claim or if the Deputy Commissioner appeals a favorable decree:

An appeal lies before the Vested Property Return Appellate Tribunal (অর্পিত সম্পত্তি প্রত্যর্পণ আপিল ট্রাইব্যুনাল) headed by a District Judge under Section 16 of the Act. Judgments of the Appellate Tribunal can be challenged before the High Court Division of the Supreme Court via Civil Revision or Constitutional Writ Petition under Article 102.

Once a final unappealable release decree is obtained:

  1. The Tribunal issues a certificate of release directed to the District Collector (DC).
  2. The DC sends an official executive order to the Assistant Commissioner (Land) to delete the property from the government's Vested Property Register (ভি-পি রেজিস্টার).
  3. The AC (Land) opens an e-Namjari mutation in the name of the successful claimant, generates an RS/BS Khatian, and accepts Land Development Tax.

faqs.question: Can an expat living in the USA, UK or Canada recover vested property without coming to Bangladesh?
faqs.answer: Yes. An overseas heir can execute a Special Power of Attorney abroad appointing an advocate or trusted representative in Bangladesh to litigate the claim before the Tribunal.

faqs.question: What happened to the 'Kha' Schedule of Vested Property?
faqs.answer: The Kha Schedule was permanently repealed and annulled by the Vested Property Return (Amendment) Act 2013. Properties in Kha schedule are free from government claim and can be mutated immediately.

faqs.question: What is the deadline for filing a case in the Vested Property Tribunal?
faqs.answer: While initial statutory deadlines expired, courts accept petitions where delayed gazette publication or lack of notice can be substantiated, or through constitutional writ petitions in the Supreme Court.

faqs.question: Can Hindu NRBs inherit and claim vested ancestral land in Bangladesh?
faqs.answer: Yes. Succession is governed by Hindu Dayabhaga personal law, and legitimate heirs have equal statutory standing under the 2001 Act to reclaim property.

faqs.question: What happens if someone else is currently leasing the vested land from the government?
faqs.answer: Under the Act, any temporary government lease automatically terminates once a final release decree is passed by the Tribunal in favor of the original owner or heir.
